instructions: Slice half the red onion as thinly as you can and put it in a small bowl of cold water. Leave it there while you chop everything else.

In a jar with a lid, add the 1/3 cup red wine vinegar, the 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 tbsp Dijon, the 2 minced garlic cloves, 1/2 tsp honey, 2 tsp oregano, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Put the lid on and shake it hard for 15 seconds.
Chop the romaine into bite-size pieces and transfer it to a large bowl. Halve the cherry tomatoes and add them.
Rinse and drain the chickpeas, then add them to the bowl. Cut the provolone into 1/4-inch cubes and the salami into bite-size pieces, and add both.
Slice 1/2 cup of the pepperoncini, drain the onion, and add both to the bowl.
To eat now, add about half the dressing and toss. Start light, since you can always add more. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

To pack lunches, divide the salad into 4 containers and the dressing into small jars. Keep them apart until you eat. The undressed salad keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days and the dressing for up to 5. Shake the dressing and toss it through right before you eat.
method_notes: Both sources dress a romaine base with chickpeas, provolone, salami and a red wine and Dijon vinaigrette, and both say to keep the dressing apart until serving. Well Plated adds kale, olives and sun-dried tomatoes; I left those out to keep it a quick lunch salad, and used its dressing ratios with a little honey. Reluctant Entertainer uses radicchio and a simpler dressing. No version had 20+ ratings (Well Plated shows 4.90 from 19; its JSON-LD also lists reviewCount 10), so this is the best-read real version.
